records.reason: Measure m125 at 0/1, 150 uL sample and 300 uL DCM. The low-loading pure-EA pair 55f2352b50967352163e and 5e1a63da794d99ec88fb retained a completion contrast, whereas measured 5/1 pairs largely converge. This extends the strong-eluent baseline across loading without assuming a constant DCM-volume correction.

Cinnamic acid at 0/1 with 2000 uL DCM provides a useful contrast to the m125 association. Compare with the 1500 uL baseline 87da8c37b16d810331a2 and the similar 2/1 endpoints in 0b247863fd6e8aaf44d8 and 9a32b65bc21fdc5f7286. This tests transfer of solvent-volume insensitivity, acknowledging the small recorded density difference.

2,6-Difluorobenzaldehyde at 20/1 and 150 uL begins a matched loading-transfer pair. At 50 uL, d2b2a221080a75b4729f measured 13.50/22.31 mL, with later onset and earlier completion than its acquisition prediction. The new prediction is 9.72/26.31; the label tests whether that endpoint mismatch extends across loading.

Complete the difluoroaldehyde pair at 50/1 and 150 uL. Together with the selected 20/1 condition and low-loading 6c28e50241ca84637c9f at 19.40/34.38 mL, this distinguishes a loading-dependent curve from a transferable correction to both endpoints.

Measure m117 at 10/1 and 150 uL. The 100 uL observation a7bc3fb68bdecbbe086f recorded V1 slightly above V2 and an exceptional onset relative to neighboring ratios. A new loading tests whether the predicted 21.62/36.44 mL response reflects a reproducible local relationship rather than transfer from that unusual label.

Pair m117 at 20/1 and 150 uL with its selected 10/1 condition. The predictor gives an onset decrease from 21.62 to 18.08 mL while completion barely changes. Measured 72231b208c5287c32d70 shows an onset reversal at 100 uL, but the independent high-loading pair is needed to assess its generality.

p-Methoxybenzaldehyde at 0/1 and 150 uL establishes a missing strong-eluent baseline for its high-loading curve. Observations de833d1e7905f1cc3be9 and ea004678fc850c759752 give 10.13/26.12 and 19.16/30.41 mL at 5/1 and 10/1. The modest 3.89/12.08 prediction tests where that response begins.

Add p-methoxybenzaldehyde at 2/1 and the same 150 uL loading. Together with the selected pure-EA baseline and measured 5/1 anchor de833d1e7905f1cc3be9, it locates the onset/completion transition without extrapolating from the exceptional low-loading 10/1 observation 2cc254396123c76b9a13.

Ethyl cinnamate at 20/1 and 100 uL starts a fixed-condition weak-eluent extension. The nearly identical 10/1 records 1142bc62e11864dd8c8f and 77f65db1224c7c295678 have completion near 16 mL. This tests the predicted rise to 22.79 mL in an aromatic conjugated ester with little measured weak-ratio coverage.

Extend the same ethyl-cinnamate series to 50/1. Its predicted 24.57/47.97 mL implies substantial growth beyond the selected 20/1 point. Measuring both points tests whether conjugation topology supports that curve, using the measured 10/1 anchors rather than assuming all aromatic esters share a weak-eluent slope.

Ethyl p-methoxybenzoate at 10/1 and 150 uL begins a ratio bridge to its measured 50/1 endpoint 8a4623d640cc619f2639, 20.16/49.15 mL. Its earlier large historical overpredictions do not establish current error. This label tests where the now-predicted moderate retention develops.

Complete the ethyl p-methoxybenzoate bridge at 20/1 and 150 uL. The selected 10/1 point, this predicted 17.53/30.63 mL point, and measured 8a4623d640cc619f2639 distinguish gradual growth from a later transition. Comparison with ethyl cinnamate tests structural transfer between different aromatic ester connectivities.

tert-Butyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 150 uL provides a loading extension of 53774efff44f690d6f30 at 100 uL. Paired with the selected 20/1 condition, it tests whether the solvent-response slope transfers across loading after ethyl acetoacetate's recent 100 uL curve was comparatively well predicted.

Measure tert-butyl acetoacetate at 20/1 and the same 150 uL loading. The prediction rises to 26.55/54.71 mL, between the moderate 10/1 anchor 53774efff44f690d6f30 and long 50/1 response 3fc05dc2025715e68174 at 100 uL. The paired labels constrain curvature and ester-substituent transfer.

Acetophenone oxime at 2/1 and 150 uL connects the new pure-EA observation eb1224edeb2e39f898b1 to the measured 20/1 high-loading endpoint a38fee52661fd3e3b7ea. Comparison with low-loading 3e41bb94c582476b5b6a tests loading transfer near the strong-eluent boundary after broad strong-eluent completion was overpredicted.

Measure the oxime at 50/1 and 150 uL. The 100 uL record 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f measured 43.11/119.20 mL, whereas the high-loading 20/1 anchor a38fee52661fd3e3b7ea is 16.43/45.70. This tests loading-dependent onset and completion growth across the weak-eluent transition, rather than selecting the large prediction for its magnitude.

Salicylaldehyde at 20/1 and 100 uL extends the newly measured same-loading curve through 10/1 in 04e162e0c1261108b4a0. Recent 1/1 and 5/1 labels rejected the pronounced predicted completion trough. This label tests subsequent growth and compares directly with the 150 uL 20/1 observation 8de30a7f5764c20b232e.

Salicylaldehyde at 5/1 and 150 uL provides a loading contrast to 61aca51ad135176924ec, 7.61/27.93 mL at 100 uL. It also connects to measured higher-loading 20/1 and 50/1 records 8de30a7f5764c20b232e and d7b688cd2da99329d657, testing whether broad moderate-ratio completion transfers across loading.

2-Phenylpyridine at 2/1 and 150 uL fills the gap between pure-EA 70714ec13048a5060224 and recent 5/1 record 1e77ce24daad192212f6. The latter's completion was underpredicted at acquisition. This locates whether the loading-dependent endpoint response already develops before the measured 5/1-to-10/1 pair.

4-Methylquinoline at 2/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between cf36dbeee8bb51632d84 and 56151359aadfa5411fc6. Their onsets decrease from 20.07 to 14.59 mL while completion stays near 34 mL. This tests an endpoint-specific loading relationship in a related basic heteroaromatic scaffold.

Ethyl benzoylacetate at 20/1 and 100 uL begins a matched weak-ratio pair. Its 5/1 observation fefecd79dc057980f62c has early onset but completion at 18.57 mL, unlike the steep ethyl-acetoacetate curve. This tests the predicted nearly flat completion response at the same loading.

Complete the ethyl-benzoylacetate pair at 50/1 and 100 uL. The predictions at 20/1 and 50/1 are approximately 6.90/19.04 and 6.54/19.12 mL. Measured f4a4fc4d6e4dea59b061 at lower loading also showed modest weak-eluent retention; the pair tests whether that topology-specific behavior generalizes across loading.

p-Bromoacetophenone at 50/1 and 100 uL extends the measured 10/1 anchor 2420964caf34a1de2a5d. Its predicted 11.99/30.08 mL can be compared with the o-bromo weak-eluent record a6f8e492c9e561c79cbd and the selected p-fluoro condition. This tests positional and halogen transfer while retaining recorded loading differences.

p-Fluoroacetophenone at 50/1 and 100 uL tests the predicted 19.94/47.87 mL extension beyond measured 7fdf49a091a855c0138f at 10/1 and bed2f1430d0964e86fcb at 20/1, 150 uL. Together with p-bromoacetophenone, it tests whether the model's different weak-eluent slopes are supported.

p-Iodoacetophenone at 50/1 and 150 uL extends e97ed592e525b9c30dec at 20/1, 14.10/29.18 mL. The new prediction, 11.23/37.63, places onset earlier despite weaker eluent. This directly tests that ordering and adds a third halogen environment without assuming a monotonic halogen effect.

Acetophenone at 20/1 and 150 uL completes a loading series with recent 79aff1183a902fa3fb7e and 380a1230c49c0a2225f3 at 50 and 100 uL. Those labels showed similar completion and decreasing onset. This common-scaffold control tests whether that modest association transfers to the remaining loading.

p-Methylacetophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL bridges measured 5/1 record 6a0f32348abbc91f704c and unusual modest 20/1 completion in ee5c9d29ed57c3312389. The prediction is 8.60/16.87 mL. It tests local curve shape after 6ece01a2e0fc9b1585df weakened the idea of broadly increasing completion with loading at 5/1.

Nitrophenethyl alcohol at 0/1 and 50 uL supplies the missing low-loading strong-eluent boundary. Compare with 6e07556df6bb6e9df96e at 100 uL and recent 97318de99bab4460cf4e at 1/1, 50 uL. This tests where the onset-loading association becomes evident before the much later 2/1 response.

The aryl pinacol boronate at 50/1 and 50 uL explores an unmeasured weak-eluent boundary with prediction 6.54/20.23 mL. Measured dc68091ba8b0648c216f and b7ebe910f1966ad518b8 show modest 5/1 and 10/1 retention at this loading. This tests transfer to the B/O environment without interpreting the exceptional high-loading 5/1 label as a general mechanism.

The formally charged P/O structure at 1/1 and 100 uL adds a strong-eluent anchor before measured d834329bf2be8835bae6 at 2/1. Its large, inconsistent 10/1 loading contrast in 902937db42f82f467718 and cb446680f62351d087a9 should not become a global charge-associated offset. This label constrains the lower-retention regime; solution speciation remains unknown.

p-Aminoacetophenone at 2/1 and 150 uL tests loading transfer from 183af335033005f96b97, 23.42/39.43 mL at 50 uL. The predicted high-loading onset is 18.15 mL. Comparison with the better-covered aminoester and heteroaromatics tests whether their onset-loading patterns extend to an aniline ketone.

Diethylaminoethyl acrylate at 2/1 and 150 uL extends 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 at 100 uL. Its 1/1 loading pair a595d5f1882c39914392 and 9a60cb4735780275034e showed a lower onset at larger loading with similar completion. This tests whether that association persists at 2/1 in a tertiary amine rather than a heteroaromatic nitrogen environment.

hypotheses.content: For m125, the association between larger recorded DCM loading-solvent volume and later completion is conditional on mobile-phase ratio. It is present at low loading under pure EA and at 1/1 and 2/1, but largely absent in the measured 5/1 loading-solvent pairs. Pure-EA loading transfer remains insufficiently tested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A constant loading-solvent-volume adjustment would misrepresent the observed ratio dependence. A higher-loading strong-eluent anchor can help constrain the interaction while limiting extrapolation from the exceptional onset records.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 300 uL DCM pure-EA baseline remain similar when sample loading increases from 50 to 150 uL?

hypotheses.content: Ester weak-eluent responses depend on connectivity and neighboring functional groups, not simply ester or acceptor counts. Recent ethyl-acetoacetate labels support substantial 10/1-to-20/1 growth, whereas malonate, acetylenic diester, and benzoylacetate observations constrain transfer of that pattern. Phenylmalonate's reproducible 20/1 anchor does not establish a reproducible 50/1 reversal.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected curves for conjugated aromatic esters, a substituted beta-ketoester, and benzoylacetate can teach different conditional slopes and prevent broad corrections from spreading across chemically distinct ester environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted weak-eluent increases for ethyl cinnamate, ethyl p-methoxybenzoate, and tert-butyl acetoacetate accurate, and does benzoylacetate retain its modest response at 100 uL?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing scaffolds occupy distinct strong-to-weak eluent regimes. At 100 uL, salicylaldehyde maintains broad completion through strong and moderate eluents without the previously predicted pronounced 5/1 trough. Oxime completion is much lower under the newly measured strong eluents, while nitroalcohol has a measured ratio-dependent onset-loading association.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The labels distinguish broad early completion from delayed onset and steep weak-eluent growth. Testing loading boundaries can prevent a single donor-based retention correction from replacing these endpoint-specific relationships.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the salicylaldehyde and oxime regimes transfer across loading, and is nitroalcohol's onset-loading association already present under pure EA?

hypotheses.content: The onset decrease predicted for m117 at 150 uL from 10/1 to 20/1 may reflect transfer from its exceptional 100 uL onset label rather than a reproducible solvent-response shape. The unusual 10/1 loading contrast in p-methoxybenzaldehyde also leaves its strong-eluent transition insufficiently constrained.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Independent condition curves can establish how strongly exceptional endpoint labels should influence neighboring ratios and related methoxyaryl aldehydes. Recorded reversed intervals warrant caution about mechanistic interpretation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m117 onset reversal recur at 150 uL, and where does the p-methoxybenzaldehyde high-loading response develop between pure EA and 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffold responses require endpoint- and ratio-specific loading conditioning. Recent 2-phenylpyridine moderate-ratio labels show modest onset differences but later high-loading completion, whereas the methylquinoline 2/1 loading contrast chiefly affects onset. Transfer to aniline ketones and tertiary aminoesters remains an untested chemical analogy.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These contrasts can distinguish a conditional onset-loading relationship from a generic basic-nitrogen correction and locate whether differences arise before moderate-ratio retention growth.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do the 2/1 responses vary across loading in phenylpyridine, methylquinoline, p-aminoacetophenone, and the tertiary aminoacrylate?

hypotheses.content: Halogenated aromatic carbonyls need local structural and endpoint-specific response models. The newly measured low-loading difluoroaldehyde curve had later onset and earlier completion than its acquisition predictions. Its loading transfer and the predictor's different weak-eluent curves for para-halogenated acetophenones remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Paired high-loading aldehyde labels and connected halogenated-ketone extensions can improve structural transfer without imposing a universal halogen effect or equating onset and completion corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the difluoroaldehyde endpoint correction persist at 150 uL, and are the predicted p-bromo, p-fluoro, and p-iodo weak-eluent response shapes supported?

feedback_interpretation:
The pure-EA m125 pair strengthened a conditional completion association: V2 was 12.85 versus 20.42 mL for 300 versus 500 uL DCM at 50 uL sample loading. Together with the larger 1/1 and 2/1 contrasts, this supports persistence under strong eluent, but the measured 5/1 pairs largely converge. I therefore retain a ratio-dependent association rather than a constant solvent-volume penalty and add only one higher-loading pure-EA baseline.

Phenylmalonate's repeated 20/1, 150 uL result, 16.97/34.91 mL, broadly agrees with the earlier 15.84/31.84 anchor; the new 100 uL result also has completion near 33 mL. This strengthens that anchor but does not validate the isolated low 50/1 result. Ethyl acetoacetate's new 100 uL 10/1 and 20/1 labels support its growing response, with especially accurate acquisition-time completion at 20/1. I shift ester effort toward other connectivities and missing response curves.

Salicylaldehyde measured completion of 25.53, 27.93, and 30.67 mL at 1/1, 5/1, and 10/1, rejecting the pronounced predicted 5/1 trough at 100 uL. The oxime strong-eluent labels instead had low completion, 9.14 mL at 0/1, 150 uL and 10.14 mL at 1/1, 100 uL, weakening broad strong-eluent donor broadening as a transferable rule. Nitroalcohol's new 1/1 low-loading onset supports a smaller onset-loading association there than at 2/1; the methoxyphenethyl-alcohol comparison does not support a universal alcohol loading effect.

The difluoroaldehyde series exposed opposite-signed acquisition errors in onset and completion, motivating a loading-transfer pair. Recent acetophenone, dibenzalacetone, chloroethyl ketone, cyclopropyl ketone, cyclohexyl phenyl ketone, aminoester, and bromobenzofuran outcomes were mostly less discrepant, so I reduce dense interpolation in those repaired regions. The p-methylacetophenone high-loading 5/1 completion was lower, weakening a broadly increasing completion-loading hypothesis. Phenylpyridine's new moderate-ratio onsets were fairly close to acquisition predictions while completion remained underpredicted by about 4–5 mL, motivating an earlier-ratio boundary. All cited errors are historical acquisition errors, not assumed current residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch concentrates on relationships that can generalize across catalog rows. Fixed-loading ratio pairs for ethyl cinnamate, ethyl p-methoxybenzoate, tert-butyl acetoacetate, benzoylacetate, and m117 distinguish response curvature from a uniform molecule-level offset. The difluoroaldehyde pair tests whether a recently observed endpoint mismatch transfers across loading. Salicylaldehyde, oxime, nitroalcohol, and nitrogen-containing scaffolds receive boundary or loading contrasts that separate onset changes from completion changes.

The para-halogenated acetophenone extensions test structural transfer in a common carbonyl family, with acetophenone and p-methylacetophenone providing useful local controls. Exploration targets specific missing condition regions: the boronate weak-eluent boundary, a strong-eluent P/O anchor, and cinnamic acid's larger loading-solvent-volume baseline. Their value comes from unresolved relationships and transfer limits, rather than chemical diversity alone.

The batch avoids spending many labels repeating recently accurate interpolations or treating isolated anomalous records as established mechanisms. Small recorded differences in density or loading solvent remain part of each comparison; no absent experimental variable is invoked to explain them. Single-predictor quantile widths are secondary evidence and are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The intended gain is better supervision of structure-condition interactions and both endpoints across the Row-distribution, not improved chromatographic performance of these selected runs.
